title: Higher Education Support Amendment (Asian Century) Bill 2013
portfolio: Tertiary Education, Skills, Science and Research

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would expand eligibility for overseas study loans and offer additional loan support to eligible university students undertaking part of their course in Asia.
The maximum loan for Asian study would rise to $7,500, with up to $1,000 extra for intensive Asian language study undertaken as preparation.
The expanded arrangements would apply from 1 January 2014 under transitional rules, with overseas study still required to count towards the student’s Australian course.
changes: Commonwealth supported postgraduate students would become eligible for overseas study loans.
Clinical placements and internships could qualify without enrolment at an overseas institution or campus.
The required study remaining after an overseas period would fall from 0.5 to 0.125 equivalent full time student load units.
Indexation of the revised maximum loan amounts would begin on 1 January 2015.
summary.affected: Eligible Commonwealth supported students, including postgraduates, and higher education providers selecting students for loans are affected.

speeches.speaker: Brett Mason
speeches.brief: The Higher Education Support Amendment (Asian Century) Bill 2013 expands OS-HELP loan eligibility for Australian students to study in Asia from 1 January 2014. The coalition supports the bill but advocates a wait-and-see approach and its own New Colombo Plan, while criticising the government's use of the guillotine to limit debate, noting 216 bills were forced through the Senate in the 43rd parliament.
